original_text: THE LAMBDA RESULT (my derivation, verified numerically for N=1,9,41 and Q from 1e-4 to 5): for a Poisson debris field with thinned intensity lambda*P_I(y)*p(y|x) and Q(x) its integral, under a scale-invariant prior p(lambda) ∝ 1/lambda the count term integrates to Gamma(N)/N!, independent of Q(x). So lambda drops out exactly, only the RELATIVE spatial variation of identification probability P_I matters (its level cancels), and absence of finds elsewhere (e.g. Western Australia) enters automatically through the denominator Q(x). This removes the obstacle at which Davey et al. stopped (p. 104). Price: the information in the count itself is given up. P_I must be modelled by coast segment AND time because coastal search effort rose after July 2015.

original_text: The drift module's tests prove a structural property of the D5 conditional likelihood prod_j q(y_j|x)/Q(x). Absolute arrival probability cancels, so particles that never beach change q and Q but not q/Q. Absence of finds counts only where identification probability P_I > 0. Example: a source sending half its items to a searched coast with no finds loses exactly 2^N over N finds; if that coast's P_I is 0 it loses nothing. Under a 1/lambda prior, an object class with no finds is uninformative, so Western Australia absence enters only through Q(x) of the classes that were found.
